newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nisshin Steel venture eyes rising demand in China.
newsitem.headline: Nisshin Steel venture eyes rising demand in China.

text.p: Japan's Nisshin Steel Co hopes to capitalise on rising Chinese demand for stainless steel by investing in a cold-rolling plant in that country, a senior company official said on Thursday.
"We have to think with a global strategy," Toshihiro Okuyama, senior managing director, said at a news conference. "In the Chinese market, stainless steel demand is rising."

Nisshin announced that it and two Japanese trade houses, Hanwa Co and Mitsui & Co, reached a basic agreement with China's Baoshan Iron and Steel Corp and Zheyong Iron and Steel Investment Co on a joint venture to build a cold-rolled mill near Ningbo, in Zhejiang province about 150 km (94 miles) south of Shanghai.
A final decision on the venture was expected by year's end.
Nisshin is to hold a 20 percent share with Hanwa and Mitsui holding a seven percent share each, while the remainder will be held by the Chinese partners.
The venture will initially construct a $150 million, 80,000 tonne-per-year cold rolling facility scheduled to begin operations in September 1998.
Okuyama said expansion of the facility was possible, although this had yet to be discussed among the partners.
He said China currently produced virtually no cold-rolled stainless steel and that the new plant was expected to supply a wide variety of domestic users.
The total level of equity investment in the venture had not yet been decided, although Okumura expected it would exceed the $150 million construction cost of the cold-rolled facility.
